connections.why: Enzymes are proteins whose tertiary structure determines their function
DNA and protein synthesis underpin how genes are controlled and expressed
Membrane structure controls transport into and out of cells and organelles
Glucose and other respiratory substrates are oxidised to release energy
Meiosis generates the genetically varied gametes inheritance depends on
Membrane transport of ions creates the resting and action potentials
Gas-exchange surfaces supply the transport systems carrying oxygen
Blood delivers metabolic waste to the kidney and liver for excretion
Hormones provide slower, longer-lasting homeostatic control such as blood glucose
Neuronal signalling is one mechanism that maintains a stable internal environment
Action potentials drive muscle contraction in animal responses
Photosynthesis stores the energy that respiration later releases as ATP
Photosynthesis fixes the energy that flows through every trophic level
Vaccines and antibodies connect to recombinant DNA technology
Inheritance of variation provides the raw material for natural selection
Classification organises the biodiversity sampled and measured in ecosystems
Gene expression and mutation underlie inherited variation
Understanding gene control enables genome editing and engineering
Cloning relies on understanding genetics and cell division
Biodiversity and population data inform conservation and sustainability
Population dynamics are studied within the ecosystems they inhabit
Xylem and phloem supply water and distribute the products of photosynthesis
